new_findings.trigger: Persist a syntactically valid existing Atlas event with its seq changed to another nonnegative safe integer. During read(), event.seq is checked for type/range but replaced with expected.seq for digest comparison; modified seq remains accepted and the returned ordered log sorts by the attacker/corruption-controlled value. Multiple events may share the same seq or be reordered without rejection.
new_findings.root_cause: The read integrity predicate checks digest of {...event,seq:expected.seq}, discarding the stored event ordinal before comparison, while appends write strictly increasing ordinals.
new_findings.criticality: Fail-closed integrity invariant of the durable event journal. This does not assert an external arbitrary attacker can edit the protected store.

proof.observed: Validation accepts altered seq except unsafe/negative, and reorder/duplicate never checked before respawnFromRecord.
proof.not_proven: No corruption injection, restarts, fresh process, or real scanner run by 208.
